ecological_question: Can isolation produce demographic source islands through reduced disturbance/competition even when graph geometry would suggest weaker incoming immigration?

ecological_contrast.published_evidence: Smith et al. used 483 individual American marten genotypes including 43 from the Apostle Islands; results supported recent island recolonization from mainland-connected recoveries, with some inferred island-to-mainland genetic movement.
ecological_contrast.measured: genotypes, kin and population genetic migration inference; NOT directly observed telemetry tracks
ecological_contrast.interpreted_explanation: islands may be refuge source because of habitat complexity, protected forest and reduced competitor effects
ecological_contrast.alternative_explanations: source history, translocations, ice bridges, environmental quality, and sampling gaps

ecological_contrast.published_evidence: Regional reintroduction study found apparent migrant population assignments but declining genetic admixture/increasing differentiation, emphasizing that movement need not imply lasting reproductive genetic integration.
ecological_contrast.endpoint_ontology: genetic immigrant signal versus effective genetic integration

future_testable_predictions: At similar Euclidean distance and coordinate-derived graph access, high local reproductive output and habitat quality predict net dispersal source status better than node centrality alone.
Occupancy and mobility records can support apparent network edges even where immigrant reproduction and persistence are absent.
Source direction may reverse over time as habitat deterioration or community pressure changes; geomatic source status alone does not identify migration direction.
Without paired viable source-output, independent movement origin-destination and reproductive integration observations, reserve claims are HOLD.

real_divergent_evidence_types.movement: independently observed departure to destination or genotype-mediated directional movement inference with caveats
real_divergent_evidence_types.conservation: demonstrable effect of source removal on recipient population persistence
